brief.meaningEn: Exceed an acceptable limit in words, actions or behaviour.
brief.meaningZh: 言語或行為越過可接受的界線，令事情從可接受變成不妥。
brief.grammar: a joke went too far; do not go too far.
brief.register: Everyday expression; explain which boundary was crossed.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是單純做得多或花時長，而是越過了具體的合理界線。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把 far 解作距離遠；也不要不說明界線便籠統批評。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出原本可接受的行為及其越界的一刻。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 19, row 6; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: The joke began to go too far when it became personal.

listening.en: The team first teased their captain about a harmless mistake, but the jokes went too far when they mentioned a private family matter in front of guests.
listening.zh: 隊員原本只是取笑隊長一個無傷大雅的錯誤，但當他們在客人面前提到私人家事時，玩笑就太過分了。
listening.promptZh: 玩笑在何時 go too far？

options.en: When it brought a private family matter into a public joke.
options.zh: 當它把私人家事變成公開笑話時。

options.en: When teammates mentioned the harmless mistake among themselves.
options.zh: 當隊員私下提起那個無傷大雅的錯誤時。

options.en: When the captain first joined the conversation.
options.zh: 當隊長首次加入對話時。

options.en: When the guests arrived, before anyone made a personal comment.
options.zh: 當客人到達、尚未有人說私人話題時。

listening.explanationZh: 界線是私事被當眾拿來開玩笑；此前取笑小失誤仍屬無傷大雅。

reply.promptEn: When should we step in during the group’s playful debate?
reply.promptZh: （小組輕鬆辯論時，我們應在甚麼情況下介入？）

options.en: When one speaker starts attacking someone’s family rather than their point.
options.zh: 當一人不再評論觀點，轉而攻擊對方家人時。

options.en: If the comments become personal, pause the discussion.
options.zh: 若評論變成人身攻擊，就暫停討論。

options.en: We should stop it if someone looks uncomfortable and asks for a break.
options.zh: 若有人感到不適並要求休息，我們應停止。

options.en: Step in when the teasing goes too far and name the boundary.
options.zh: 當取笑變得過分時介入，指出被越過的界線。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都提出合理介入時機；金句用 go too far 概括越界並要求說明界線。

scene.promptZh: 同學先互相開玩笑，後來有人把另一位同學的病歷當笑料。哪句最貼切？

options.en: The teasing went too far when it turned a private medical detail into a joke.
options.zh: 取笑把私人醫療資料變成笑料時，就太過分了。

options.en: The teasing went too far only because the class was nearly over, not because of the private detail.
options.zh: 玩笑過火只因快下課，而不是因為提及私事。

options.en: The speaker meant to be funny, so the private detail may not count as crossing a boundary.
options.zh: 說話者本意是開玩笑，因此或許不算越過私隱界線。

scene.explanationZh: 私人醫療資料被當作笑料，顯示行為越過尊重私隱的界線。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不適合說 someone went too far？

options.en: A friendly debate turns into repeated insults about a classmate’s background.
options.zh: 友善辯論演變成反覆侮辱同學背景。

options.en: Two friends share a mild joke they both enjoy and stop before bringing up personal matters.
options.zh: 兩位朋友互相開一個都覺得好笑的輕鬆玩笑，並在觸及私事前停止。

options.en: A reviewer criticises a performance and then shares unrelated private messages.
options.zh: 評論者先評表演，後公開與表演無關的私人訊息。

contrast.explanationZh: 雙方都享受輕鬆玩笑，而且在觸及私事前停止，沒有越界；持續侮辱或公開私訊則已越界。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「我接受對我的簡報提出意見，但他把我的家庭問題放進公開評論。」哪句回應最貼切？

options.en: That went too far; feedback on your slides did not require sharing private family details.
options.zh: 那太過分了；評論投影片並不需要公開私人家事。

options.en: The comment may have started as feedback, but the family detail is probably a separate issue to raise later.
options.zh: 評論或許由簡報意見開始，但家庭私事可能要另行處理。

options.en: I would ask him to focus on the slides next time, without discussing the private comment now.
options.zh: 我會請他下次集中評論投影片，暫時不談今次公開私事的問題。

dialogue.explanationZh: 朋友接受簡報意見，卻不接受公開家庭私事；合適回應要明確指出今次已跨越私隱界線，不能只留待下次。

speaking.en: The criticism went too far when the reviewer quoted a private message unrelated to the play.
speaking.zh: 評論者引用與劇作無關的私人訊息時，批評便太過分了。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出哪個動作越過了合理界線。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：圖書館讀書會原本友善地評論一本小說，後來一人公開朗讀作者的私人電郵。用一至兩句英文說明越界之處及可行的處理。
writing.selfCheckZh: 說清原本評論小說是可接受的、公開私人電郵越界，以及應停止或回到作品討論。

examples.en: The discussion went too far when someone read the author’s private email aloud; the chair should stop that and return to the novel.
examples.zh: 有人大聲讀出作者私人電郵時，討論便太過分了；主持人應制止，讓大家回到小說。

examples.en: Criticising the novel was fair, but reading a private email went too far, so the group should focus on the book instead.
examples.zh: 評論小說本來公平，但朗讀私人電郵就太過分了，因此小組應重新聚焦作品。

takeaways.en: The interview went too far when the host pressed for details about a family dispute.
takeaways.zh: 主持人追問家庭爭執細節時，訪問便太過分了。

takeaways.en: A joke can go too far when it reveals information shared in confidence.
takeaways.zh: 玩笑若洩露別人私下告知的資料，就可能太過分。

brief.meaningEn: Excessive admiration that treats a person as almost beyond criticism.
brief.meaningZh: 過度崇拜某個人，將對方理想化到難以接受批評。
brief.grammar: hero worship of a singer; appreciation can become hero worship.
brief.register: Often critical; distinct from ordinary appreciation of talent or work.
brief.boundaryZh: 核心是對某個人的理想化，與一般欣賞不同；不一定涉及對某機構的忠誠。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把任何支持名人的行為都說成 hero worship；要有過度理想化的證據。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出欣賞何時演變成無法理性評價偶像。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 19, row 7; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: The interview moved from appreciation into hero worship.

listening.en: The young musician admired the violinist’s technique. Later, he insisted she could never make a poor choice and copied even her unrelated opinions. His admiration had become hero worship.
listening.zh: 年輕樂手欣賞小提琴家的技巧。後來，他堅稱她不可能作出差的選擇，連與音樂無關的意見也照單全收；欣賞已變成偶像崇拜。
listening.promptZh: 甚麼行為顯示 hero worship？

options.en: He treats the violinist as incapable of error beyond her musical skill.
options.zh: 他不只欣賞技藝，還認定小提琴家在其他方面也不會犯錯。

options.en: He studies her bowing technique and asks informed questions.
options.zh: 他研究她的運弓技巧，提出有根據的問題。

options.en: He decides to attend one of her performances.
options.zh: 他決定去看她一場演出。

options.en: He compares her recordings with those of other players.
options.zh: 他把她的錄音與其他演奏家比較。

listening.explanationZh: 認定偶像所有選擇都不可能錯，超出了對演奏技巧的正常欣賞。

reply.promptEn: Why are the fans rejecting every review of their favourite actor?
reply.promptZh: （影迷為何拒絕閱讀所有對喜愛演員的評論？）

options.en: They believe he can do nothing badly.
options.zh: 他們認為他做甚麼都不會差。

options.en: They take criticism of his performance as a personal attack.
options.zh: 他們把對演出的批評當作人身攻擊。

options.en: Their hero worship leaves no room for a balanced view of his work.
options.zh: 他們的偶像崇拜令他們無法平衡地看待他的作品。

options.en: They prefer praise without discussing the performances themselves.
options.zh: 他們只想聽讚美，不願討論演出本身。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋拒絕評論；金句指出對演員的過度理想化。

scene.promptZh: 學生欣賞一位作家，但逐漸聲稱作家每本書都完美，任何評論者都不配提出意見。哪句最貼切？

options.en: His appreciation has turned into hero worship.
options.zh: 他的欣賞已變成偶像崇拜。

options.en: He is a devoted reader who still accepts that reviewers may have reasons for criticism.
options.zh: 他是忠實讀者，但仍接受評論者可能有批評的理由。

options.en: He rejects one review because it misquotes the book, while still allowing other criticism.
options.zh: 他因一篇評論錯引書中文字而反對它，但仍接受其他批評。

scene.explanationZh: 將作家每部作品視為完美，並拒絕批評，顯示理想化崇拜。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不適合稱為 hero worship？

options.en: A fan insists their idol can never be wrong about anything.
options.zh: 歌迷堅稱偶像任何事情都不會錯。

options.en: A reader admires a poet’s work but accepts that some poems are weaker.
options.zh: 讀者欣賞詩人的作品，也承認部分詩作較弱。

options.en: A follower repeats every opinion a celebrity expresses without examining it.
options.zh: 追隨者不加思索地重複名人的每個看法。

contrast.explanationZh: 欣賞之餘仍能評價作品優劣，沒有把詩人理想化。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「我喜歡她的歌，但有些新歌不合我口味。」哪句最能說明這是否屬於 hero worship？

options.en: That is appreciation without hero worship; you can enjoy her work and still judge it.
options.zh: 那是沒有盲目崇拜的欣賞；你可以喜歡她的作品，也作出自己的判斷。

options.en: You can admire her music strongly and explain why those particular songs do not work for you.
options.zh: 你可以非常欣賞她的音樂，同時說明那些歌為何不合你口味。

options.en: That sounds like a difference in taste rather than proof that the singer has no skill.
options.zh: 那像是口味不同，不足以證明歌手沒有能力。

dialogue.explanationZh: 朋友既欣賞歌手也保留判斷，最能說明他並非盲目崇拜；喜好與歌手能力是相關但較窄的問題。

speaking.en: Hero worship began to replace thoughtful listening when every comment about the singer was treated as an insult.
speaking.zh: 當任何對歌手的評論都被當成侮辱，偶像崇拜便開始取代審慎聆聽。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出歌迷在哪裏失去獨立判斷。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：電影社有同學很欣賞一位導演，但現在堅稱她每部電影都完美，拒絕聽任何有理據的影評。用一至兩句英文描述欣賞如何變質及可作的改變。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出同學原本欣賞導演、現在認定每部作品完美並拒絕有理據的批評；提出平衡看法。

examples.en: His admiration for the director has become hero worship: he calls every film perfect and should consider well-supported reviews.
examples.zh: 他對導演的欣賞已成偶像崇拜：他認為每部電影都完美，應考慮有理據的影評。

examples.en: Hero worship keeps him from hearing fair criticism of the director’s films, so he should judge each work on its own merits.
examples.zh: 偶像崇拜令他聽不進對導演電影的合理批評；他應按每部作品本身作出評價。

takeaways.en: Hero worship can make a fan confuse admiration with unquestioning approval.
takeaways.zh: 偶像崇拜會令歌迷把欣賞與無條件贊同混為一談。

takeaways.en: A respectful interview can avoid hero worship by asking thoughtful questions.
takeaways.zh: 尊重嘉賓之餘提出審慎問題，可避免把訪問變成偶像崇拜。

lessons.titleEn: keep your feet on the ground
lessons.titleZh: 保持務實、不被沖昏頭腦

brief.meaningEn: Remain realistic and sensible despite success, praise or excitement.
brief.meaningZh: 即使獲得成功或讚美，仍能務實看待下一步，不被興奮沖昏頭腦。
brief.grammar: keep your feet on the ground after a win; she kept her feet on the ground.
brief.register: Encouraging advice; it does not mean refusing to celebrate.
brief.boundaryZh: 重點是成功後仍保有現實判斷，不必壓抑喜悅，也不是叫人站在地上。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把謙虛寫成否認成就；應說明如何保持務實。
brief.outcomeZh: 能同時承認好消息和指出接下來要做的事。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 19, row 11; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: It is wise to keep your feet on the ground after a big win.
sources.expression: keep your feet on the ground

listening.en: After winning the regional contest, the robotics team celebrated, then checked the parts that still failed in testing. Their coach said they had kept their feet on the ground.
listening.zh: 機械人隊贏得地區賽後慶祝，隨後檢查測試中仍出故障的零件。教練說他們保持了務實態度。
listening.promptZh: 教練為甚麼這樣評價隊伍？

options.en: They enjoyed the win while still attending to remaining problems.
options.zh: 他們享受勝利，同時繼續處理尚存問題。

options.en: They celebrated the win but postponed discussing a known design weakness.
options.zh: 他們慶祝勝利，卻延後討論已知的設計弱點。

options.en: They began the next project without checking the judges’ suggestions.
options.zh: 他們沒有查看評審建議，就開始下一個計劃。

options.en: They focused on the praise and treated the remaining tests as optional.
options.zh: 他們只看讚賞，並把剩餘測試當成可做可不做。

listening.explanationZh: 隊伍一方面慶祝，另一方面仍處理已知不足；推遲檢討、忽略建議或只看讚賞，都欠缺腳踏實地的平衡。

reply.promptEn: How should the band respond after its first concert sells out?
reply.promptZh: （樂隊第一場音樂會售罄後應如何應對？）

options.en: Celebrate, then rehearse the passages that still need work.
options.zh: 先慶祝，再練習仍需改善的段落。

options.en: Thank the audience and keep planning for the next concert.
options.zh: 感謝觀眾，並繼續籌劃下一場。

options.en: Enjoy the moment while listening to honest feedback.
options.zh: 享受這一刻，同時聽取真誠意見。

options.en: Keep your feet on the ground and prepare carefully for the next show.
options.zh: 保持務實，認真準備下一場演出。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都是合理做法；金句用本課表達概括興奮之餘仍務實準備。

scene.promptZh: 學生作品獲獎後，她感謝評審、與朋友慶祝，也按評語修訂作品。哪句最貼切？

options.en: She kept her feet on the ground after winning the prize.
options.zh: 她得獎後仍保持務實。

options.en: She appreciated the award but waited until much later to read the judges’ feedback.
options.zh: 她感謝獎項，卻到很久以後才閱讀評審意見。

options.en: She revised the work only after another contest required changes.
options.zh: 她只在另一場比賽要求修改時才修訂作品。

scene.explanationZh: 獲獎後即按評語修訂，顯示她既肯定成就又繼續改進；延後或被動修改較不足以表達此平衡。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個做法最不符合 keep your feet on the ground？

options.en: A player celebrates a win and still trains for the next match.
options.zh: 球員慶祝勝利，也繼續為下一場練習。

options.en: A founder receives praise but checks the next project’s budget.
options.zh: 創辦人獲讚賞，仍核查下一項計劃的預算。

options.en: A singer decides one successful show means no more rehearsals are needed.
options.zh: 歌手認定一場成功演出代表以後無需排練。

contrast.explanationZh: 把一次成功當成日後毋須準備，失去現實判斷。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「我的短片獲讚賞，我很高興，但下次還想改善收音。」哪句回應最貼切？

options.en: You are keeping your feet on the ground: enjoy the praise and improve the sound.
options.zh: 你保持務實：享受讚賞，也改善收音。

options.en: You could enjoy the praise first and put off the sound review for a while.
options.zh: 你可以先享受讚賞，把收音檢討押後一段時間。

options.en: The audience liked the film, so the sound issue may be less urgent than you think.
options.zh: 觀眾喜歡短片，所以收音問題或許沒你想像中急切。

dialogue.explanationZh: 朋友既享受讚賞，又主動改善收音；回應應肯定這種平衡，不能只推遲檢討或淡化已知問題。

speaking.en: Even after the prize, she kept her feet on the ground and asked how to improve the next film.
speaking.zh: 即使得獎，她仍保持務實，詢問下一部電影可以如何改進。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出她如何在得獎後繼續學習。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：學校辯論隊首次贏得決賽，大家很興奮，但下星期還要參加另一場比賽，並需改善反駁技巧。用一至兩句英文給隊員建議。
writing.selfCheckZh: 承認決賽勝利及興奮，並提出下星期賽前要練習反駁；保持務實不等於不慶祝。

examples.en: Celebrate the final, but keep your feet on the ground and practise rebuttals before next week’s contest.
examples.zh: 慶祝決賽勝利，但要保持務實，在下星期比賽前練習反駁。

examples.en: The team can enjoy its first win and keep its feet on the ground by reviewing weak rebuttals for the next competition.
examples.zh: 隊伍可以享受首次勝利，並透過檢討薄弱的反駁，務實準備下一場比賽。

takeaways.en: After her first exhibition sold out, the artist kept her feet on the ground and planned the next one carefully.
takeaways.zh: 首次展覽售罄後，藝術家仍保持務實，細心籌備下一個展覽。

takeaways.en: You can keep your feet on the ground and still be proud of your achievement.
takeaways.zh: 你可以保持務實，同時為自己的成就感到自豪。

brief.meaningEn: Deliberately place a subtle hint in a story so it becomes meaningful later.
brief.meaningZh: 作者有意在故事較早處安插不顯眼的提示，讓讀者後來回看時發現其意義。
brief.grammar: plant a tiny clue in the opening; planted a tiny clue early.
brief.register: Narrative and mystery-writing phrase; implies intention and later relevance.
brief.boundaryZh: 線索須刻意埋下且後來有用；普通背景細節或意外透露答案都不同。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把 plant 解成種植物，也不要讓線索在開頭直接揭穿結局。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出小提示、後來的揭示，以及兩者如何呼應。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 22, row 5; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: The author chose to plant a tiny clue in the opening chapter.

listening.en: In chapter one, the author mentions a scratched brass key on the desk. Only at the end do we learn it opens the locked studio. She planted a tiny clue early in the story.
listening.zh: 作者在第一章提到桌上一把刮花的黃銅鑰匙；到結尾我們才知道它能打開鎖上的畫室。她很早便埋下小伏筆。
listening.promptZh: 黃銅鑰匙如何成為 tiny clue？

options.en: It appears quietly early on and matters to the later reveal.
options.zh: 它早早低調出現，之後的揭示才顯出重要性。

options.en: The key is mentioned early, but it never matters when the studio is opened.
options.zh: 鑰匙在故事早段出現，卻與後來打開工作室無關。

options.en: A key appears shortly before the reveal, leaving little earlier hint for readers.
options.zh: 鑰匙在揭曉前不久才出現，讀者此前幾乎得不到提示。

options.en: The early scene shows the key and directly explains what it opens.
options.zh: 早段場面展示鑰匙，也直接說明它會打開哪裏。

listening.explanationZh: 細小線索須早於揭曉出現，當時不完全說破，後來又有用；沒有後續作用、出現太遲或太早解釋都不符合。

reply.promptEn: How can we make the ending feel fair without revealing the secret too early?
reply.promptZh: （我們怎樣讓結尾合理，又不過早揭穿秘密？）

options.en: Mention an ordinary-looking object that gains meaning later.
options.zh: 提及一件後來才顯出意義的普通物件。

options.en: Give readers one detail they can recognise on a second reading.
options.zh: 給讀者一個重讀時能認出的細節。

options.en: Let a brief early description connect with the final discovery.
options.zh: 讓開頭一段簡短描述與最後的發現呼應。

options.en: Plant a tiny clue in the opening scene, then explain it near the end.
options.zh: 在開場埋下一個小伏筆，接近結尾時再解釋。

reply.explanationZh: 四項都能令結局有跡可循；金句直接用本課表達講安插小提示。

scene.promptZh: 故事開頭有人順手把藍色紐扣放入口袋；結尾才知道紐扣來自失蹤者的外套。哪句最貼切？

options.en: The writer planted a tiny clue with the blue button.
options.zh: 作者以藍色紐扣埋下了一個小伏筆。

options.en: The button appears near the ending, just before its owner is named.
options.zh: 鈕扣接近結尾才出現，緊接着就公布物主。

options.en: The opening points out the button’s exact owner, leaving nothing to infer later.
options.zh: 開頭便點明鈕扣屬誰，其後無須推理。

scene.explanationZh: 鈕扣在開頭看似普通，到結尾才與失蹤者連起來；若太遲出現或立即說破，就失去埋線索的作用。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不適合說 the writer planted a tiny clue？

options.en: An odd date in an early letter later exposes the false alibi.
options.zh: 早期信件裏一個奇怪日期後來揭穿不在場證明。

options.en: A briefly seen scarf later identifies the visitor.
options.zh: 早前一閃而過的圍巾後來證實訪客身份。

options.en: A page states the culprit’s name and method before the investigation starts.
options.zh: 調查開始前，一頁文字已直接寫出犯人姓名和手法。

contrast.explanationZh: 直接揭穿犯人並非不顯眼的小提示；其餘兩項早期細節後來才顯出作用。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「我重看開頭才發現，那張寫錯的車票其實暗示主角上錯了車。」哪句回應最貼切？

options.en: The writer planted a tiny clue in the ticket, so the later reveal feels earned.
options.zh: 作者在車票埋下小伏筆，令後來的揭示有跡可循。

options.en: The ticket may be relevant, but the writer might have made its meaning clear too early.
options.zh: 車票可能有關，但作者或許太早說明其意義。

options.en: Perhaps the ticket was introduced only just before the reveal, rather than in the opening.
options.zh: 或許車票只在揭曉前不久才出現，而不是在開頭。

dialogue.explanationZh: 朋友說重看開頭才發現車票暗示後來的結果，符合早段細微提示與後段呼應；不是揭曉前才加入，也非一開始說破。

speaking.en: The playwright planted a tiny clue when a character checked the station clock twice.
speaking.zh: 劇作家讓角色兩度看車站時鐘，藉此埋下一個小伏筆。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出哪個小動作可能成為伏筆。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你寫一篇推理故事，開頭提到一位訪客手上的綠色墨跡；結尾讀者才知道失竊地圖是用綠墨修改的。用一至兩句英文描述你如何安排伏筆。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出開頭不起眼的綠墨跡，以及結尾它如何連到被修改的失竊地圖；不可在開頭直接說明真相。

examples.en: I planted a tiny clue by mentioning green ink on the visitor’s hand; only at the end does it link to the altered stolen map.
examples.zh: 我提到訪客手上的綠墨跡，埋下一個小伏筆；到結尾它才與被修改的失竊地圖連上關係。

examples.en: The opening plants a tiny clue in the visitor’s ink-stained hand, which gains meaning when the stolen map’s green edits are revealed.
examples.zh: 故事開頭在訪客沾墨的手埋下一個小伏筆；失竊地圖的綠色改動揭示後，它才顯出意義。

takeaways.en: A mystery can plant a tiny clue in a casual remark that matters later.
takeaways.zh: 推理故事可在一句隨口的話裏埋下日後有用的小伏筆。

takeaways.en: She planted a tiny clue on page two without revealing the answer.
takeaways.zh: 她在第二頁埋下一個小伏筆，沒有揭穿答案。
